counterfactual_missing_items: No histopathological evidence of squamous differentiation (e.g., keratin pearls) or basaloid nests
No mention of actinic keratosis or solar damage supporting squamous cell carcinoma
No nodular or pigmented features typical of basal cell carcinoma beyond dermoscopic findings
decisive_items: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified (hematoxylin-eosin staining, original magnification ×40)
Patient had history of kidney transplant in 2004 causing immunocompromised status.
response.rationale: R3 directly matches the definitive histopathological finding of intracellular yeasts with halos in an immunocompromised host, which is pathognomonic for cryptococcosis. R5 and R4 rely on non-specific clinical/dermoscopic features (ulceration, telangiectasias) that are contradicted by the yeast identification. C1 is a redundant append-only variant of R3 with no additional raw evidence.

rejected.why: Clinical features of ulceration and telangiectasias are non-specific and contradicted by the histopathological yeast finding; no squamous differentiation evidence.
Dermoscopic features suggest BCC but are overridden by the definitive yeast histopathology; no basaloid nests or peripheral palisading described.
Redundant append-only completion of R3 with identical raw support; adds no new evidence and is subsumed by R3.
